At a local minimum beta, the upper comparison must be at least beta along any feasible path. Multiplication by positive M(p) gives max_z[tau_cz(p)-beta M(p)] at least zero. All finitely many old terms vanish, so the right derivative of the maximum is the maximum of their derivatives with no missing normalizing factor in the inequality.

For a fixed selection of linear rows on an open parameter domain, strict separation of the finite convex hull from zero would make every row negative on one allowed direction. The same reasoning works for rows in each closed convex hull: negative evaluation persists on approximating finite convex combinations, one of whose original rows must be negative. Choosing one such row at every base contradicts the universal selection inequality. With one deepest site each individual row is therefore zero.
